tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Weak maximum principle for mixed boundary data] 1. ch8:8.98\group ch08-generalized-solutions Assume (8.5), (8.6), and \begin{equation} \int _\Omega (dv-b^iD_iv)\, dx-\int _\Gamma \sigma v\, ds\leq 0 \quad \forall v\geq 0,\quad v\in C_0^1(\Omega \cup \Gamma ). \tag {8.98} \end{equation} If $u\in W^{1,2}(\Omega )$ satisfies \[ \Lop (u,v)+\int _\Gamma \sigma uv\, ds\leq 0 \] for every nonnegative $v\in W_0^{1,2}(\Omega \cup \Gamma )$, then either \[ \sup _\Omega u\leq \sup _{\Gamma _D}u^+ \] or $u$ is a positive constant.
Proof

\sketch Repeat the truncation argument of Theorem 8.1 with test functions vanishing on $\Gamma _D$. Condition (8.98) controls the interior and conormal zeroth-order terms. The only exceptional case left by the support-measure argument is a positive constant.

□
